---
title: "Step 7 - Phylogenetic tree"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# Preparations

Load the necessary libraries

```{r libraries}
library(ape)          #for trees, rooting and plotting
library(phangorn)     #for protein distances and bootstrap
```

# Read the alignment

The trimmed alignment from Step 6 (MUSCLE + Gblocks on Phylogeny.fr).

```{r readData}
aln <- read.phyDat("alignment_clean.aln",
                   format = "fasta", type = "AA")
aln
```

# Neighbour-joining tree

The sequences are proteins, so I used a protein substitution model (JTT)
instead of the DNA model (JC69) used in the practical.

```{r nj}
dm <- dist.ml(aln, model = "JTT")
nj_tree <- nj(dm)

# set negative branch lengths to 0 (as in the Week 3 practical)
nj_tree$edge.length[nj_tree$edge.length < 0] <- 0
```

# Root the tree with the outgroup

```{r root}
OG <- "OUTGROUP_Escherichia_coli_536_Q0TA78.1"
rooted_tree <- root(nj_tree, outgroup = OG, resolve.root = TRUE)
```

# Bootstrap support

100 bootstrap replicates: the alignment columns are resampled and a new NJ tree
is made each time. The number on a node is how many of the 100 trees had that group.

```{r bootstrap}
set.seed(123)
bs <- bootstrap.phyDat(aln, FUN = function(x) nj(dist.ml(x, model = "JTT")), bs = 100)
support <- prop.clades(rooted_tree, bs, rooted = FALSE)
```

# Plot the tree

Representative sequences are shown in red.

```{r plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
rooted_tree$tip.label <- gsub("_", " ", rooted_tree$tip.label)
tip_colours <- ifelse(grepl("^Group", rooted_tree$tip.label), "red", "black")

plot(rooted_tree, cex = 0.6, no.margin = TRUE, tip.color = tip_colours)
nodelabels(support, frame = "none", cex = 0.5, adj = c(1.2, -0.3))
add.scale.bar(cex = 0.6)

png("tree.png", width = 2000, height = 1800, res = 250)
plot(rooted_tree, cex = 0.6, no.margin = TRUE, tip.color = tip_colours)
nodelabels(support, frame = "none", cex = 0.5, adj = c(1.2, -0.3))
add.scale.bar(cex = 0.6)
dev.off()

write.tree(rooted_tree, "tree.nwk")
```
